72:   putreg32(NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_CLKSOURCE | NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_TICKINT |

84:    */

89:   priority &= ~NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR15_MASK;
90:   priority |= NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT <<
91:               NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR15_SHIFT;
92:   putreg32(priority, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
93: 
94:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);

96:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT);

34: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM  0xb2000000u
35: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT   0xb3000000u
36: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL   0xb4000000u

52: static int bk7258_smp_boot_send(int cpu, uint32_t command)
53: {
54:   uint32_t data[2] = {command, 0};
55:   int retry;
56: 
57:   UP_DMB();
58:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
59:     {
60:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
61: 
62:       if (ret == OK)
63:         {
64:           return OK;
65:         }
66: 
67:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
68:         {
69:           return ret;
70:         }
71: 
72:       __asm__ volatile("nop");

78: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
79: {
80:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
81:   int expected = 0;
82:   int retry;
83: 
84:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
85:     {
86:       return -EINVAL;
87:     }
88: 
89:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY | (pending & 0xffu));
90:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
91:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
92:     {
93:       bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | 0x100u);
94:       return OK;
95:     }
96: 
97:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | (cpu & 0xffu));
98:   UP_DMB();
99:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
100:     {
101:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
102: 
103:       if (ret == OK)
104:         {
105:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT | (retry & 0xffffu));
106:           return OK;
107:         }
108: 
109:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
110:         {
111:           atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
112:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL |
113:                            ((uint32_t)(-ret) & 0xffffu));

115:         }
116: 
117:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
118:     }

120:   atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
121:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL | 0xffffu);
122:   return -ETIMEDOUT;

129:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)

132:         {

134:         }

137:     }

139:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
140:     {
141:       if (cpu == 1)
142:         {
143:           atomic_set_release(&g_boot_ping_received, 1);
144:           if (bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
145:               BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK)

173:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 AP_SPINLOCK-backed software hwspinlock.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h>
12: 
13: #include "arm_internal.h"
14: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
15: 
16: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY       0xa1000000u
17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 && (bk7258_boottrace_words()[6] & 0xffu) == 2u)
39:     {
40:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */
93: 
94:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
95:   UP_DMB();
96:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
99: 
100:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
101:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
102:     {
103:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
104:       UP_DMB();
105:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
106:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
112:   UP_DMB();
113:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
114:   return true;
115: }
116: 
117: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
118: {
119:   (void)dev;
120:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
121: }
122: 
123: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
124: {
125:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
126: 
127:   (void)dev;
128:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
129:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
130:     {
131:       PANIC();
132:     }
133: 
134:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
135:     {
136:       UP_DMB();
137:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
138:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
143:   UP_DMB();
144:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
145:   UP_DSB();
146:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
147:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
148: }
149: 
150: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
151: {
152:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
153:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
154:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
155: };
156: 
157: void bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize(void)
158: {
159:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[0] = 0;
160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
164:   UP_DSB();
165:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
166: }

39: /****************************************************************************

41:  ****************************************************************************/
42: 
43: /* The SysTick is driven by watchdog tock clock. */
44: 
45: #define SYSTICK_CLOCK BOARD_TICK_CLOCK
46: 
47: /* The desired timer interrupt frequency is provided by the definition
48:  * CLK_TCK (see include/time.h).  CLK_TCK defines the desired number of
49:  * system clock ticks per second.  That value is a user configurable setting
50:  * that defaults to 100 (100 ticks per second = 10 MS interval).
51:  */
52: 
53: #define SYSTICK_RELOAD ((SYSTICK_CLOCK / CLK_TCK) - 1)
54: 
55: /* The size of the reload field is 24 bits.  Verify that the reload value
56:  * will fit in the reload register.
57:  */
58: 
59: #if SYSTICK_RELOAD > 0x00ffffff
60: #  error SYSTICK_RELOAD exceeds the range of the RELOAD register
61: #endif
62: 
63: /****************************************************************************
64:  * Private Functions
65:  ****************************************************************************/
66: 
67: /****************************************************************************
68:  * Function:  rp2040_timerisr
69:  *
70:  * Description:
71:  *   The timer ISR will perform a variety of services for various portions
72:  *   of the systems.
73:  *
74:  ****************************************************************************/
75: 
76: static int rp2040_timerisr(int irq, uint32_t *regs, void *arg)
77: {
78:   /* Process timer interrupt */
79: 
80:   nxsched_process_timer();
81:   return 0;
82: }
83: 
84: /****************************************************************************
85:  * Public Functions
86:  ****************************************************************************/
87: 
88: /****************************************************************************
89:  * Function:  up_timer_initialize
90:  *
91:  * Description:
92:  *   This function is called during start-up to initialize
93:  *   the timer interrupt.
94:  *
95:  ****************************************************************************/
96: 
97: void up_timer_initialize(void)
98: {
99:   uint32_t regval;
100: 
101:   /* Set the SysTick interrupt to the default priority */
102: 
103:   regval = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3);
104:   regval &= ~SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_15_MASK;
105:   regval |= (NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT << SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_15_SHIFT);
106:   putreg32(regval, ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3);
107: 
108:   /* Configure SysTick to interrupt at the requested rate */
109: 
110:   putreg32(SYSTICK_RELOAD, ARMV6M_SYSTICK_RVR);
111:   putreg32(0, ARMV6M_SYSTICK_CVR);
112: 
113:   /* Attach the timer interrupt vector */
114: 
115:   irq_attach(RP2040_IRQ_SYSTICK, (xcpt_t)rp2040_timerisr, NULL);
116: 
117:   /* Enable SysTick interrupts. */
118: 
119:   putreg32((SYSTICK_CSR_TICKINT | SYSTICK_CSR_ENABLE), ARMV6M_SYSTICK_CSR);
120: 
121:   /* And enable the timer interrupt */
122: 
123:   up_enable_irq(RP2040_IRQ_SYSTICK);
124: }

49: /****************************************************************************
50:  * Function:  esp32_timerisr
51:  *
52:  * Description:
53:  *   The timer ISR will perform a variety of services for various portions
54:  *   of the systems.
55:  *
56:  *   Xtensa timers work by comparing a cycle counter with a preset value.
57:  *   Once the match occurs an interrupt is generated, and the handler has to
58:  *   set a new cycle count into the comparator.  To avoid clock drift due to
59:  *   interrupt latency, the new cycle count is computed from the old, not the
60:  *   time the interrupt was serviced. However if a timer interrupt is ever
61:  *   serviced more than one tick late, it is necessary to process multiple
62:  *   ticks until the new cycle count is in the future, otherwise the next
63:  *   timer interrupt would not occur until after the cycle counter had
64:  *   wrapped (2^32 cycles later).
65:  *
66:  ****************************************************************************/
67: 
68: static int esp32_timerisr(int irq, uint32_t *regs, void *arg)
69: {
70:   uint32_t divisor;
71:   uint32_t compare;
72:   uint32_t diff;
73: 
74:   divisor = g_tick_divisor;
75:   do
76:     {
77:       /* Increment the compare register for the next tick */
78: 
79:       compare = xtensa_getcompare();
80:       xtensa_setcompare(compare + divisor);
81: 
82:       /* Process one timer tick */
83: 
84:       nxsched_process_timer();
85: 
86:       /* Check if we are falling behind and need to process multiple timer
87:        * interrupts.
88:        */
89: 
90:       diff = xtensa_getcount() - compare;
91:     }
92:   while (diff >= divisor);
93: 
94:   return OK;
95: }
96:

107:  *
108:  ****************************************************************************/

111: {
112:   uint32_t divisor;
113:   uint32_t count;
114: 
115:   /* Configured the timer0 as the system timer.
116:    *
117:    *   divisor = BOARD_CLOCK_FREQUENCY / ticks_per_sec
118:    */
119: 
120:   divisor = BOARD_CLOCK_FREQUENCY / CLOCKS_PER_SEC;
121:   g_tick_divisor = divisor;
122: 
123:   /* Set up periodic timer */
124: 
125:   count = xtensa_getcount();
126:   xtensa_setcompare(count + divisor);

129:    * attach any peripheral ID to the dedicated CPU interrupt.

52: /****************************************************************************
53:  * Name:  nxsched_cpu_scheduler
54:  *
55:  * Description:
56:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
57:  *   active task on one CPU.
58:  *
59:  * Input Parameters:
60:  *   cpu - The CPU that we are performing the scheduler operations on.
61:  *
62:  * Returned Value:
63:  *   None
64:  *
65:  ****************************************************************************/
66: 
67: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
68: static inline void nxsched_cpu_scheduler(int cpu)
69: {
70:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
71: 
72: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
73:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses round robin scheduling. */
74: 
75:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
76:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR)
77:     {
78:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
79:        * timeslice.
80:        */
81: 
82:       nxsched_process_roundrobin(rtcb, 1, false);
83:     }
84: #endif
85: 
86: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
87:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses sporadic scheduling. */
88: 
89:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
90:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
91:     {
92:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
93:        * budget.
94:        */
95: 
96:       nxsched_process_sporadic(rtcb, 1, false);
97:     }
98: #endif
99: }
100: #endif
101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name:  nxsched_process_scheduler
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
107:  *   active task on all configured CPUs.
108:  *
109:  * Input Parameters:
110:  *   None
111:  *
112:  * Returned Value:
113:  *   None
114:  *
115:  ****************************************************************************/
116: 
117: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
118: static inline void nxsched_process_scheduler(void)
119: {
120:   irqstate_t flags;
121:   int i;
122: 
123:   /* Single CPU case:
124:    * For nested interrupts, higher IRQs may interrupt nxsched_cpu_scheduler()
125:    * but nxsched_cpu_scheduler() requires that interrupts be disabled.
126:    * We are in ISR context, no meaning we are disabled the interrupts.
127:    *
128:    * SMP case:
129:    * enter_critical_section() does much more than just disable interrupts on
130:    * the local CPU; it also manages spinlocks to assure the stability of the
131:    * TCB that we are manipulating.
132:    */
133: 
134:   flags = enter_critical_section();
135: 
136:   /* Perform scheduler operations on all CPUs */
137: 
138:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; i++)
139:     {
140:       nxsched_cpu_scheduler(i);
141:     }
142: 
143:   leave_critical_section(flags);
144: }
145: #else
146: #  define nxsched_process_scheduler()
147: #endif
148:

150:  * Public Functions
151:  ****************************************************************************/
152: 
153: /****************************************************************************
154:  * System Timer Hooks
155:  *
156:  * These are standard interfaces that are exported by the OS
157:  * for use by the architecture specific logic
158:  *
159:  ****************************************************************************/
160: 
161: /****************************************************************************
162:  * Name:  nxsched_process_timer
163:  *
164:  * Description:
165:  *   This function handles system timer events.
166:  *   The timer interrupt logic itself is implemented in the
167:  *   architecture specific code, but must call the following OS
168:  *   function periodically -- the calling interval must be
169:  *   USEC_PER_TICK
170:  *
171:  * Input Parameters:
172:  *   None
173:  *
174:  * Returned Value:
175:  *   None
176:  *
177:  ****************************************************************************/
178: 
179: void nxsched_process_timer(void)
180: {
181: #ifdef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
182:   /* Process wall time */
183: 
184:   clock_update_wall_time();
185: #endif
186: 
187:   /* Increment the system time (if in the link) */
188: 
189:   clock_timer();
190: 
191:   /* Check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
192:    * timeslice.
193:    */
194: 
195:   nxsched_process_scheduler();
196: 
197:   /* Process watchdogs */
198: 
199:   wd_timer(clock_systime_ticks());
200: 
201: #ifdef CONFIG_SYSTEMTICK_HOOK
202:   /* Call out to a user-provided function in order to perform board-specific,
203:    * custom timer operations.
204:    */
205: 
206:   board_timerhook();
207: #endif
208: }

40: /****************************************************************************
41:  * Name:  nxsched_process_delivered
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *    This function is used to process the tcb in g_delivertasks.
45:  * 1 We use direct locking instead of enter_critical_section
46:  * to save processing time
47:  * 2 If there is a higher priority task, we will still perform
48:  * the higher priority task
49:  * 3 If the schedule lock is on, the task will be placed in g_pendingtasks
50:  *
51:  * Input Parameters:
52:  *   cpu
53:  *
54:  * Returned Value:
55:  *   OK
56:  *
57:  * Assumptions:
58:  * - The caller must be in irq
59:  * - current cpu must not be locked
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: void nxsched_process_delivered(int cpu)
64: {
65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;
67: 
68:   DEBUGASSERT(up_interrupt_context());
69: 
70:   flags = enter_critical_section();
71:   priority = per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu);
72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;
73: 
74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&
75:       !nxsched_switch_running(cpu, priority == SWITCH_EQUAL))
76:     {
77:       /* Manage the (rare) case that task delivery to this CPU was not
78:        * successful. This can happen in two cases:
79:        * 1) The currently running task on this CPU just entered sched_lock
80:        * 2) This CPU just picked a higher priority task to execute
81:        *    before this SMP call was executed
82:        * To avoid schedule latency/priority inversion, just check once more
83:        * if there is another CPU eglible to run the delivered task, and
84:        * pass it forward.
85:        */
86: 
87:       FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
88:       if (tcb)
89:         {
90:           int target_cpu = tcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ?
91:             tcb->cpu : nxsched_select_cpu(tcb->affinity);
92:           if (target_cpu != cpu &&
93:               current_task(target_cpu)->sched_priority < tcb->sched_priority)
94:             {
95:               nxsched_deliver_task(cpu, target_cpu, priority);
96:             }
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:   leave_critical_section(flags);
101: }

191: int nxsched_smp_call_handler(int irq, FAR void *context,
192:                              FAR void *arg)
193: {
194:   FAR sq_queue_t *call_queue;
195:   FAR sq_entry_t *curr;
196:   FAR sq_entry_t *next;
197:   int cpu = this_cpu();
198: 
199:   irqstate_t flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
200: 
201:   call_queue = &g_smp_call_queue[cpu];
202: 
203:   sq_for_every_safe(call_queue, curr, next)
204:     {
205:       FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data =
206:         container_of(curr, struct smp_call_data_s, node[cpu]);
207:       FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *cookie;
208:       int ret;
209: 
210:       sq_rem(&data->node[cpu], call_queue);
211: 
212:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
213: 
214:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
215: 
216:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
217: 
218:       cookie = data->cookie;
219:       if (cookie != NULL)
220:         {
221:           if (ret < 0)
222:             {
223:               cookie->error = ret;
224:             }
225: 
226:           /* Insert ack back to original cpu call queue,
227:            * add direct avoid nxsched_smp_call_add g_smp_call_lock again.
228:            */
229: 
230: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
231:           sq_addlast(&cookie->ack.node[cookie->cpu],
232:                      &g_smp_call_queue[cookie->cpu]);
233:           up_send_smp_call(1 << cookie->cpu);
234: #else
235:           nxsem_post(&cookie->sem);
236: #endif
237:         }
238:     }
239: 
240:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
241:   return OK;
242: }

222:         }
223: 
224:       desc->used = false;
225:     }
226: 
227:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
228:     {
229:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
230:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
231:       g_processing_order = 0;
232:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
233:         {
234:           break;
235:         }
236: 
237:       desc->used = false;
238:     }
239: }
240: 
241: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
242: {
243:   uintptr_t rdata0;
244:   uintptr_t rdata1;
245:   uintptr_t sidreg;
246:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
247:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
248: 
249:   (void)irq;
250:   (void)context;
251:   (void)arg;
252: 
253:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
254:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
255:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
256:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
257:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
258:     {
259:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
260:     }
261:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
262:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
263:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
264: 
265:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
266:     {
267:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
268:       uint32_t address;
269:       uint32_t length;
270:       uint8_t source;
271: 
272:       if (cpu == 0)
273:         {
274:           mbox_process_desc();
275:         }
276: 
277:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
278:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
279:         {
280:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
281:           mbox_trace_errors();
282:           break;
283:         }
284: 
285:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
286:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
287:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
288: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
289:       if (length == 0)
290:         {
291:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
292:             {
293:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
294:                 {
295:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
296:                 }
297: 
298:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
299:             }
300:           else
301:             {
302:               if (cpu == 0)
303:                 {
304:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
305:                   mbox_trace_errors();
306:                 }
307:             }
308: 
309:           continue;
310:         }
311: #endif
312: 
313:       if (cpu != 0)
314:         {
315:           continue;
316:         }
317: 
318:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
319:         {
320:           continue;
321:         }
322: 
323:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
324:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
325:              sizeof(desc->message));
326:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
327:       desc->used = true;
328:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
329:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
330:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
331:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
332:       mbox_process_desc();
333:     }
334: 
335:   if (cpu == 0)
336:     {
337:       mbox_process_desc();
338:     }
339: 
340:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
341:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
342:     {
343:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
344:     }
345: 
346:   return OK;
347: }
348: 
349: void bk7258_mbox_set_callback(bk7258_mbox_callback_t callback)
350: {
351:   g_callback = callback;
352: }
353: 
354: void bk7258_mbox_kick_rx(void)
355: {
356:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
357: 
358:   (void)bk7258_mbox_irq(0, NULL, NULL);
359:   up_irq_restore(flags);
360: }
361: 
362: void bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred(void)
363: {
364:   unsigned int i;
365: 
366:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
367:     {
368:       if (g_rx_desc[i].used && g_processing_order != 0 &&
369:           (int32_t)(g_rx_desc[i].order - g_processing_order) < 0 &&
370:           !mbox_priority_message(&g_rx_desc[i].message))
371:         {
372:           g_rx_desc[i].used = false;
373:         }
374:     }
375: }
376: 
377: void bk7258_mbox_get_stats(struct bk7258_mbox_stats *stats)
378: {
379:   irqstate_t flags;
380: 
381:   if (stats == NULL)
382:     {
383:       return;
384:     }
385: 
386:   flags = up_irq_save();
387:   *stats = g_stats;
388:   up_irq_restore(flags);
389: }
390: 
391: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
392: {
393:   int ret;
394: 
395:   if (g_mbox_ready)
396:     {
397:       return OK;
398:     }
399: 
400:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
401:   g_rx_order = 0;
402:   g_processing_order = 0;
403:   memset(&g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
404: 
405:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
406:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are
407:    * then processed normally instead of being blindly discarded.
408:    */
409: 
410:   putreg32(2u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
411:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
412:             BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG);
413:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
414: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
415:   putreg32(5u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
416:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
417:             BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG);
418:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH2_FIFO_CFG);
419: #endif
420:   modifyreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);
421:   mbox_clear_errors(0);
422: 
423:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);
424:   if (ret < 0)
425:     {
426:       return ret;
427:     }
428: 
429:   g_mbox_ready = true;
430: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
431:   g_mbox_smp_ready = true;
432: #endif
433:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
434:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
435:   return OK;
436: }
437: 
438: bool bk7258_mbox_smp_ready(void)
439: {
440: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
441:   return g_mbox_ready && g_mbox_smp_ready;
442: #else
443:   return false;
444: #endif
445: }
446: 
447: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
448: int bk7258_mbox_secondary_init(void)
449: {
450:   if (!g_mbox_ready || !g_mbox_smp_ready || up_cpu_index() != 1)
451:     {
452:       return -EAGAIN;
453:     }
454: 
455:   mbox_clear_errors(1);
456:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
457:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
458:   return OK;
459: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 CPU2 startup.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>
9: #include <stdbool.h>
10: #include <stdint.h>
11: #include <syslog.h>
12: 
13: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
14: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>
15: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
16: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
17: #include <nuttx/sched_note.h>
18: 
19: #include "arm_internal.h"
20: #include "dwt.h"
21: #include "init/init.h"
22: #include "nvic.h"
23: #include "sched/sched.h"
24: #include "hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h"
25: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
26: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
27: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
28: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
29: 
30: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS != 2
31: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP supports exactly two AP CPUs"
32: #endif
33: 
34: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ != 480000000
35: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP requires the fixed 480 MHz CP contract"
36: #endif
37: 
38: #define BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES  (CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / 2u)
39: #define BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT     4000000u
40: 
41: extern uint8_t __secondary_vectors_start[];
42: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_base[];
43: 
44: static void bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset(void)
45: {
46:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
47:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
48:   UP_DSB();
49: }
50: 
51: static void bk7258_cpu2_release_reset(void)
52: {
53:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
54:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
55:   UP_DSB();
56:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
57: }
58: 
59: static void __attribute__((used, noreturn)) bk7258_secondary_idle(void)
60: {
61:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
62:   arm_initialize_stack();
63:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_STACK);
64:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);
65:   bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
66:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
67:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ_ON);
68:   up_irq_enable();
69:   sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
70:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_SCHED);
71: 
72:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_ping_received())
73:     {
74:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
75:     }
76: 
77:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_WAIT);
78:   bk7258_smp_boot_ack();
79:   bk7258_smp_secondary_ready();
80:   nx_idle_trampoline();
81:   PANIC();
82: }
83: 
84: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
85: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
86:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
87: {
88:   __asm__ volatile
89:     (
90:       "msr psp, r0\n"
91: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
92:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
93: #endif
94:       "mrs r1, control\n"
95:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
96:       "msr control, r1\n"
97:       "isb sy\n"
98:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
99:     );
100: }
101: 
102: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
103:                            target("general-regs-only")))
104: bk7258_secondary_boot(void)
105: {
106:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
107:   uintptr_t idle_top;
108: 
109:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ENTRY);
110:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
111:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
112:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
113:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
114:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
115:     {
116:       PANIC();
117:     }
118: 
119:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
120: 
121:   tcb = current_task(1);
122:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
123:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);
124: }
125: 
126: void __attribute__((naked, noreturn, section(".start_text")))
127: bk7258_secondary_start(void)
128: {
129:   __asm__ volatile
130:     (
131:       "cpsid i\n"
132:       "movs r0, #1\n"
133:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
134:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
135:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
136:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
137:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
138:     );
139: }
140: 
141: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
142: {
143:   irqstate_t flags;
144:   uint32_t started;
145:   uint32_t polls = 0;
146:   uint32_t control;
147:   uint32_t status;
148:   bool ping_sent = false;
149: 
150:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
151: 
152:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
153:     {
154:       return -EINVAL;
155:     }
156: 
157:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
158:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
159:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
160:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
161:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
162:     {
163:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
164:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
165:       PANIC();
166:     }
167: 
168:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
169:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
170:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
171:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
172:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
173:     {
174:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
175:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
176:       PANIC();
177:     }
178: 
179:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
180:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
181:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
182: 
183:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
184:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
185:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
186:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
187:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
188:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
189:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
190:   UP_DMB();
191:   UP_DSB();
192: 
193:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
194:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
195:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
196:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
197:   flags = up_irq_save();
198:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
199:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
200:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
201:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
202: 
203:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
204:     {
205:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
206:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
207:         {
208:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
209:             {
210:               break;
211:             }
212: 
213:           ping_sent = true;
214:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
215:         }
216: 
217:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
218:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
219:         {
220:           break;
221:         }
222:     }
223: 
224:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
225:     {
226:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
227:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
228:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
229:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
230:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
231:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
232:       up_irq_restore(flags);
233:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
234:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
235:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
236:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
237:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
238:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
239:       PANIC();
240:     }
241: 
242:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
243:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
244:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
245:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
246:   UP_DSB();
247:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
248:   up_irq_restore(flags);
249:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
250:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
251:   return OK;
252: }

107: void __attribute__((noinline, target("general-regs-only")))
108: bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(bool primary)
109: {
110:   const size_t region_count = sizeof(g_bk7258_mpu_regions) /
111:                               sizeof(g_bk7258_mpu_regions[0]);
112: 
113:   if (!primary)
114:     {
115:       arm_fpuconfig();
116:     }
117: 
118:   putreg32(0, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x08);
119:   putreg32(0x00000000u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x0c);
120:   putreg32(0x0fffffe3u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x10);
121:   putreg32(1, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x08);
122:   putreg32(0x10000000u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x0c);
123:   putreg32(0xefffffe1u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x10);
124:   putreg32(1, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x00);
125:   UP_DSB();
126:   UP_ISB();
127: 
128:   putreg32((uintptr_t)__ram_vectors_start, NVIC_VECTAB);
129:   UP_DSB();
130:   UP_ISB();
131: 
132: #ifdef CONFIG_ARM_MPU
133:   {
134:     const uint32_t hardware_regions =
135:       (getreg32(MPU_TYPE) & MPU_TYPE_DREGION_MASK) >>
136:       MPU_TYPE_DREGION_SHIFT;
137: 
138:     if (hardware_regions < region_count)
139:       {
140:         for (; ; )
141:           {
142:             __asm__ volatile("wfi");
143:           }
144:       }
145: 
146:     mpu_reset();
147:     mpu_initialize(g_bk7258_mpu_regions, region_count, false, true);
148: 
149:   }
150: #endif
151: 
152:   (void)primary;
153: }
154: 
155: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
156:                            target("general-regs-only")))
157: bk7258_start(void)
158: {
159:   const uint8_t *src;
160:   uint8_t *dest;
161: 
162:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_C);
163: 
164:   /* Configure the FPU before code compiled for the hard-float ABI can use
165:    * it.  arm_fpuconfig() does not depend on BSS-backed synchronization.
166:    */
167: 
168:   arm_fpuconfig();
169:   UP_DSB();
170:   UP_ISB();
171:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_CPACR);
172: 
173:   for (src = _eronly, dest = _sdata; dest < _edata; )
174:     {
175:       *dest++ = *src++;
176:     }
177: 
178:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_DATA);
179: 
180:   for (dest = _sbss; dest < _ebss; )
181:     {
182:       *dest++ = 0;
183:     }
184: 
185:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_BSS);
186: 
187:   for (src = __ram_vectors_load, dest = __ram_vectors_start;
188:        dest < __ram_vectors_end; )
189:     {
190:       *dest++ = *src++;
191:     }
192: 
193:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_VECTORS);
194: 
195: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
196:   bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize();
197: #endif
198:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_SPINLOCK);
199:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(true);
200:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_PRIVATE);
201:   arm_initialize_stack();
202: 
203:   /* Install the buffered AP log channel before normal NuttX startup. */
204:   (void)bk7258_syslog_initialize();

206: #ifdef USE_EARLYSERIALINIT
207:   arm_earlyserialinit();
208: #endif
209: 
210:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_NXSTART);
211:   nx_start();
212:   for (; ; )
213:     {
214:     }
215: }

222:       "movs r0, #0\n"
223:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
224:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
225:       "ldr r1, =0x2800ffe0\n"
226:       "ldr r2, =0x41505452\n"
227:       "str r2, [r1]\n"
228:       "movs r2, #1\n"
229:       "str r2, [r1, #4]\n"
230:       "movs r2, #0\n"
231:       "str r2, [r1, #8]\n"
232:       "str r2, [r1, #12]\n"
233:       "str r2, [r1, #16]\n"
234:       "str r2, [r1, #20]\n"
235:       "str r2, [r1, #24]\n"

641:  * Name: rspin_lock/rspin_lock_irqsave/rspin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt
642:  *
643:  * Description:
644:  *   Nest supported spinlock, can support UINT16_MAX max depth.
645:  *   As we should not disable irq for long time, sched also locked.
646:  *   Similar feature with enter_critical_section, but isolate by instance.
647:  *
648:  *   If SPINLOCK is enabled:
649:  *     Will take spinlock each cpu first call.
650:  *
651:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:
652:  *     Equivalent to up_irq_save() + sched_lock().
653:  *     Will only sched_lock once when first called.
654:  *
655:  *   NOTE: This function is only allowed to execute with irq disabled.
656:  *
657:  * Input Parameters:
658:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s. not NULL.
659:  *
660:  * Returned Value:
661:  *   An opaque, architecture-specific value that represents the state of
662:  *   the interrupts prior to the call to spin_lock_irqsave(lock);
663:  *
664:  ****************************************************************************/
665: 
666: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
667: static inline_function
668: void rspin_lock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
669: {
670:   rspinlock_t new_val;
671:   rspinlock_t old_val;
672:   int         cpu = this_cpu() + 1;
673: 
674:   /* Already owned this lock. */
675: 
676:   old_val.val = atomic_read(&lock->val);
677: 
678:   if (old_val.owner == cpu)
679:     {
680:       lock->count += 1;
681:     }
682:   else
683:     {
684:       /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
685: 
686:       spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
687: 
688:       /* Try seize the ownership of the lock using CAS. */
689: 
690:       new_val.count = 1;
691:       new_val.owner = cpu;
692: 
693:       do
694:         {
695:           old_val.val = 0;
696:         }
697:       while (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->val,
698:              &old_val.val, new_val.val));
699: 
700:       /* Mark locked only when the lock is acquired for the first time. */
701: 
702:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
703:     }
704: }

713: }

174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: up_cpu_start
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
179:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
180:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
181:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
182:  *
183:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
184:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
185:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
186:  *   initialized.
187:  *
188:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
189:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
190:  *
191:  * Input Parameters:
192:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
193:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
194:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
195:  *
196:  * Returned Value:
197:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
202: {
203:   int i;
204:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
205:   uint32_t core1_boot_msg[5];
206: 
207:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
208: 
209: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
210:   /* Notify of the start event */
211: 
212:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
213: #endif
214: 
215:   /* Reset Core 1 */
216: 
217:   setbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
218:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF) & RP2040_PSM_PROC1))
219:     ;
220:   clrbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
221: 
222:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
223: 
224:   /* Send initial VTOR, MSP, PC for Core 1 boot */
225: 
226:   core1_boot_msg[0] = 0;
227:   core1_boot_msg[1] = 1;
228:   core1_boot_msg[2] = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_VECTAB);
229:   core1_boot_msg[3] = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
230:                                 tcb->adj_stack_size;
231:   core1_boot_msg[4] = (uint32_t)core1_boot;
232:

234:     {
235:       fifo_drain();
236:       for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)

254: 
255:   /* CPU Core 1 boot done */
256: 
257:   spin_unlock(&g_core1_boot);
258: 
259:   return 0;
260: }

176: 		}

178: 		BK_ASSERT((core_id == 0) || (core_id  == 1));

178: /**
179:  * @brief Peterson algorithm (shared memory) implementation for spinlock protection between AP and CP
180:  * 
181:  * Since AP side is an SMP system, when AP subsystem enters exception, it first acquires SMP system spinlock,
182:  * then shuts down the other core. AP and CP are AMP system, this solution mainly describes using Peterson
183:  * algorithm (shared memory) to implement spinlock protection between AP and CP.
184:     ________________________________________
185:     1. Objectives
186:     • SMP CP/AP share a section of SRAM (fixed address), when any subsystem enters exception:
187:     o First arrival monopolizes UART → DUMP system info → direct reboot (without releasing lock);
188:     o Later arrival waits permanently (WFE()), avoiding UART conflicts.
189:     • Ensure reliable fallback solution even when shared area is corrupted.
190: 
191:     ________________________________________
192:     2. Shared memory layout (fixed address macros)
193:     • MAGIC_BEGIN / MAGIC_END: Header/tail magic numbers for validating shared area legitimacy.
194:     • CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS / AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS: Peterson's want[0]/want[1].
195:     • EXCEPTION_TURN: turn in Peterson algorithm.
196:     • EXCEPTION_DUMPER: marks who holds the lock (0=CP, 1=AP, -1=none); also used for "first come first serve DUMP" in fallback.
197:     ________________________________________
198: 
199:  */
200:

204: static inline void cpu_sev(void){ __asm volatile("sev" ::: "memory"); }

213:     if (!(turn==0u || turn==1u)) return 0;
214:     if (!(dump== TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER || dump==0 || dump==1)) return 0;

83: /****************************************************************************
84:  * Private Functions
85:  ****************************************************************************/
86: 
87: /****************************************************************************
88:  * Name: clock_basetime
89:  *
90:  * Description:
91:  *   Get the initial time value from the best source available.
92:  *
93:  ****************************************************************************/
94: 
95: #ifdef CONFIG_RTC
96: #if defined(CONFIG_RTC_DATETIME)
97: /* Initialize the system time using a broken out date/time structure */
98: 
99: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
100: {
101:   struct tm rtctime;
102:   long nsecs = 0;
103:   int ret;
104: 
105:   /* Get the broken-out time from the date/time RTC. */
106: 
107: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_RTC_SUBSECONDS
108:   ret = up_rtc_getdatetime_with_subseconds(&rtctime, &nsecs);
109: #else
110:   ret = up_rtc_getdatetime(&rtctime);
111: #endif
112:   if (ret >= 0)
113:     {
114:       /* And use the broken-out time to initialize the system time */
115: 
116:       tp->tv_sec  = timegm(&rtctime);
117:       tp->tv_nsec = nsecs;
118:     }
119: 
120:   return ret;
121: }
122: 
123: #elif defined(CONFIG_RTC_HIRES)
124: 
125: /* Initialize the system time using a high-resolution structure */
126: 
127: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
128: {
129:   /* Get the complete time from the hi-res RTC. */
130: 
131:   return up_rtc_gettime(tp);
132: }
133: 
134: #else
135: 
136: /* Initialize the system time using seconds only */
137: 
138: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
139: {
140:   /* Get the seconds (only) from the lo-resolution RTC */
141: 
142:   tp->tv_sec  = up_rtc_time();
143:   tp->tv_nsec = 0;
144:   return OK;
145: }
146: 
147: #endif /* CONFIG_RTC_HIRES */
148: #else /* CONFIG_RTC */
149: 
150: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
151: {
152:   time_t jdn = 0;
153: 
154:   /* Get the EPOCH-relative julian date from the calendar year,
155:    * month, and date
156:    */
157: 
158:   jdn = clock_calendar2utc(CONFIG_START_YEAR, CONFIG_START_MONTH - 1,
159:                            CONFIG_START_DAY);
160: 
161:   /* Set the base time as seconds into this julian day. */
162: 
163:   tp->tv_sec  = jdn * (time_t)SEC_PER_DAY;
164:   tp->tv_nsec = 0;
165:   return OK;
166: }
167: 
168: #endif /* CONFIG_RTC */
169: 
170: /****************************************************************************
171:  * Name: clock_inittime
172:  *
173:  * Description:
174:  *   Get the initial time value from the best source available.
175:  *
176:  ****************************************************************************/
177: 
178: #ifdef CONFIG_RTC
179: static void clock_inittime(FAR const struct timespec *tp)
180: {
181:   /* (Re-)initialize the time value to match the RTC */
182: 
183: #ifndef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
184:   struct timespec ts;
185:   irqstate_t flags;
186: 
187:   clock_systime_timespec(&ts);
188: 
189:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
190:   if (tp)
191:     {
192:       memcpy(&g_basetime, tp, sizeof(struct timespec));
193:     }
194:   else
195:     {
196:       clock_basetime(&g_basetime);
197:     }
198: 
199:   /* Adjust base time to hide initial timer ticks. */
200: 
201:   g_basetime.tv_sec  -= ts.tv_sec;
202:   g_basetime.tv_nsec -= ts.tv_nsec;
203:   while (g_basetime.tv_nsec < 0)
204:     {
205:       g_basetime.tv_nsec += NSEC_PER_SEC;
206:       g_basetime.tv_sec--;
207:     }
208: 
209:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
210:   clock_notifier_call_chain(CLOCK_REALTIME, &g_basetime);
211: #else
212:   clock_inittimekeeping(tp);
213: #endif
214: }
215: #endif

267: /****************************************************************************
268:  * Name: clock_synchronize
269:  *
270:  * Description:
271:  *   Synchronize the system timer to a hardware RTC.  This operation is
272:  *   normally performed automatically by the system during clock
273:  *   initialization.  However, the user may also need to explicitly re-
274:  *   synchronize the system timer to the RTC under certain conditions where
275:  *   the system timer is known to be in error.  For example, in certain low-
276:  *   power states, the system timer may be stopped but the RTC will continue
277:  *   keep correct time.  After recovering from such low-power state, this
278:  *   function should be called to restore the correct system time.
279:  *
280:  *   Calling this function could result in system time going "backward" in
281:  *   time, especially with certain lower resolution RTC implementations.
282:  *   Time going backward could have bad consequences if there are ongoing
283:  *   timers and delays.  So use this interface with care.
284:  *
285:  * Input Parameters:
286:  *   tp: rtc time should be synced, set NULL to re-get time
287:  *
288:  * Returned Value:
289:  *   None
290:  *
291:  * Assumptions:
292:  *
293:  ****************************************************************************/
294: 
295: #ifdef CONFIG_RTC
296: void clock_synchronize(FAR const struct timespec *tp)
297: {
298:   /* Re-initialize the time value to match the RTC */
299: 
300:   clock_inittime(tp);
301: }
302: #endif
303: 
304: /****************************************************************************
305:  * Name:  clock_synchronize_monotonic
306:  *
307:  * Description:
308:  *   Synchronize the system boottime with remote hardware server.
309:  *
310:  * Input Parameters:
311:  *   tp: boot time should be synced.
312:  *
313:  * Returned Value:
314:  *   None
315:  *
316:  * Assumptions:
317:  *
318:  ****************************************************************************/
319: 
320: #ifndef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
321: void clock_synchronize_monotonic(FAR const struct timespec *tp)
322: {
323:   irqstate_t flags;
324:   struct timespec ts;
325: 
326:   /* Re-initialize the time value to match the RTC */
327: 
328:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
329: 
330:   clock_systime_timespec(&ts);
331:   g_monotonic_basetime.tv_sec = tp->tv_sec - ts.tv_sec;
332:   g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec = tp->tv_nsec - ts.tv_nsec;
333:   if (g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec < 0)
334:     {
335:       g_monotonic_basetime.tv_sec -= 1;
336:       g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec += NSEC_PER_SEC;
337:     }
338: 
339:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
340: }
341: #endif
342: 
343: /****************************************************************************
344:  * Name: clock_resynchronize
345:  *
346:  * Description:
347:  *   Resynchronize the system timer to a hardware RTC.  The user can
348:  *   explicitly re-synchronize the system timer to the RTC under certain
349:  *   conditions where the system timer is known to be in error.  For example,
350:  *   in certain low-power states, the system timer may be stopped but the
351:  *   RTC will continue keep correct time.  After recovering from such
352:  *   low-power state, this function should be called to restore the correct
353:  *   system time. Function also keeps monotonic clock at rate of RTC.
354:  *
355:  *   Calling this function will not result in system time going "backward" in
356:  *   time. If setting system time with RTC would result time going "backward"
357:  *   then resynchronization is not performed.
358:  *
359:  * Input Parameters:
360:  *   rtc_diff:  amount of time system-time is adjusted forward with RTC
361:  *
362:  * Returned Value:
363:  *   None
364:  *
365:  * Assumptions:
366:  *
367:  ****************************************************************************/
368: 
369: #if defined(CONFIG_RTC) && !defined(CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS) && \
370:     !defined(CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING) && !defined(CONFIG_ALARM_ARCH) && \
371:     !defined(CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH)
372: void clock_resynchronize(FAR struct timespec *rtc_diff)
373: {
374:   struct timespec rtc_time;
375:   struct timespec bias;
376:   struct timespec curr_ts;
377:   struct timespec rtc_diff_tmp;
378:   irqstate_t flags;
379:   int ret;
380: 
381:   if (rtc_diff == NULL)
382:     {
383:       rtc_diff = &rtc_diff_tmp;
384:     }
385: 
386:   /* Get RTC time */
387: 
388:   ret = clock_basetime(&rtc_time);
389:   if (ret < 0)
390:     {
391:       /* Error reading RTC, skip resynchronization. */
392: 
393:       sinfo("rtc error %d, skip resync\n", ret);
394: 
395:       rtc_diff->tv_sec = 0;
396:       rtc_diff->tv_nsec = 0;
397:       return;
398:     }
399: 
400:   /* Set the time value to match the RTC */
401: 
402:   /* Get the elapsed time since power up (in milliseconds).  This is a
403:    * bias value that we need to use to correct the base time.
404:    */
405: 
406:   clock_systime_timespec(&bias);
407: 
408:   /* Add the base time to this.  The base time is the time-of-day
409:    * setting.  When added to the elapsed time since the time-of-day
410:    * was last set, this gives us the current time.
411:    */
412: 
413:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
414:   clock_timespec_add(&bias, &g_basetime, &curr_ts);
415:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
416: 
417:   /* Check if RTC has advanced past system time. */
418: 
419:   if (curr_ts.tv_sec > rtc_time.tv_sec ||
420:       (curr_ts.tv_sec == rtc_time.tv_sec &&
421:        curr_ts.tv_nsec >= rtc_time.tv_nsec))
422:     {
423:       /* Setting system time with RTC now would result time going
424:        * backwards. Skip resynchronization.
425:        */
426: 
427:       sinfo("skip resync\n");
428: 
429:       rtc_diff->tv_sec = 0;
430:       rtc_diff->tv_nsec = 0;
431:     }
432:   else
433:     {
434:       /* Output difference between time at entry and new current time. */
435: 
436:       clock_timespec_subtract(&rtc_time, &curr_ts, rtc_diff);
437: 
438:       /* Add the sleep time to correct system timer */
439: 
440:       clock_t diff_ticks = SEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_sec) +
441:                            NSEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_nsec);
442: 
443:       flags = write_seqlock_irqsave(&g_system_tick_lock);
444:       g_system_ticks += diff_ticks;
445:       write_sequnlock_irqrestore(&g_system_tick_lock, flags);
446:     }
447: }
448: #endif
449: 
450: /****************************************************************************
451:  * Name: clock_timer
452:  *
453:  * Description:
454:  *   This function must be called once every time the real time clock
455:  *   interrupt occurs.  The interval of this clock interrupt must be
456:  *   USEC_PER_TICK
457:  *
458:  ****************************************************************************/
459: 
460: #if !defined(CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS) && \
461:     !defined(CONFIG_ALARM_ARCH) && !defined(CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH)
462: void clock_timer(void)
463: {
464:   irqstate_t flags;
465: 
466:   /* Increment the per-tick system counter */
467: 
468:   flags = write_seqlock_irqsave(&g_system_tick_lock);
469:   g_system_ticks++;
470:   write_sequnlock_irqrestore(&g_system_tick_lock, flags);
471: }
472: #endif

136:  *
137:  * Description:
138:  *   This is a primitive counting synchronization mechanism

145:  *   irqstate

149: static inline_function
150: irqstate_t write_seqlock_irqsave(FAR seqcount_t *s)
151: {
152:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
153: 
154: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
155:   for (; ; )
156:     {
157:       uint32_t sequence = atomic_read(&s->sequence);
158: 
159:       if (predict_true((sequence & 1u) == 0u))
160:         {
161:           /* Try to acquire the lock ownership. */
162: 
163:           if (atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&s->sequence, &sequence, sequence + 1u))
164:             {
165:               break;
166:             }
167:         }
168: 
169:       /* CPU Relax and retry. */
170:     }
171: #else
172:   s->sequence++;
173: #endif
174: 
175:   return flags;
176: }

    nuttx/atomic: use toolchain builtin atomic function
    
    The reason for using builtin atomic is that in C++, when include <atomic> in <nuttx/atomic.h> easily conflicts with third-party function libraries. We wanted to completely separate the implementation of <nuttx/atomic.h>.
    
    There are two points:
    1. use builtin function directly.
    2. Without the standard library implementation, need implement "atomic_fetch_xxx", leading conflicts with the standard library used by third-party programs, introducing redefinition issues and requiring name changes.
    
    Signed-off-by: zhangyu117 <[REDACTED-INTERNAL-EMAIL]>

**Overall Conclusion**

The current BK7258 design is correct in one central respect: logical CPU0 should own the only system tick, and its SysTick ISR should call `nxsched_process_timer()` directly. Moving scheduler/timer processing to a worker, idle loop, or deferred thread is not a valid minimal fix.

The highest-risk divergence from established NuttX SMP ports is the fallible mailbox IPI path. NuttX effectively assumes that once `up_send_smp_sched()` or `up_send_smp_call()` returns, the target CPU will eventually enter the SMP interrupt handler. BK7258 can silently leave pending work without a delivered interrupt, especially CPU1-to-CPU0 traffic.

**High-Risk Findings**

1. **CPU1-to-CPU0 IPI failure can strand scheduler work or SMP calls indefinitely.**

BK sets the pending bit, makes up to 1024 mailbox attempts, then clears `g_ipi_kicked` while retaining the pending bit on failure: [bk7258_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:78).

Only CPU0’s tick retries pending traffic, and only for target CPU1: [bk7258_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:206). There is no equivalent progress mechanism for pending target CPU0 traffic.

This matters because:

- `nxsched_deliver_task()` records remote work and ignores the return from `up_send_smp_sched()`: [sched.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:489).
- `up_send_smp_call()` has no return value at all: [arch.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/arch.h:2427).
- A synchronous SMP call waits for completion after queuing: [sched_smp.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:312).

By comparison:

- RP2040 waits until the inter-core FIFO accepts the doorbell: [rp2040_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_smpcall.c:150).
- ESP32 writes a level-style inter-CPU interrupt register with no fallible return path: [esp32_intercpu_interrupt.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32/esp32_intercpu_interrupt.c:103).
- CXD56 similarly uses a non-failing interrupt-set register: [cxd56_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/cxd56xx/cxd56_smpcall.c:167).

Safe minimal direction: make mailbox doorbell acceptance effectively guaranteed for every online target. A dedicated level-triggered interrupt register would be preferable. If FIFO is the only option, wait until accepted, or treat a health-bounded failure as fatal rather than silently returning. Do not rely on the CPU0 tick as the general retry engine.

2. **The current SMP/atomic implementation is not reproducible from the recorded Git commits.**

At current `HEAD` `ab949cc`, these central files are untracked:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_atomic.c`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c`

Commit `eaf469f` enabled SMP and added these filenames to CMake, but the files themselves are absent from that commit’s tree. Therefore neither `eaf469f` nor `55e315e` records the current SMP implementation, and a clean checkout cannot reproduce the presently linked image.

3. **The enabled ticket-spinlock mode depends on an uncommitted NuttX core fix.**

The BK generated configuration has `CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK=y`: [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:411).

The contest NuttX tree locally changes ticket `spin_trylock_notrace()` to use a private expected value: [spinlock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:256). The clean `openvela/nuttx` copy instead passes `&lock->owner` to compare-exchange: [spinlock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:256).

Because failed compare-exchange updates its expected argument, the clean implementation can corrupt `lock->owner`. The local fix is technically justified and required if ticket spinlocks remain enabled, but it is not committed in the NuttX repository.

**Tick Contract**

`nxsched_process_timer()` is the architecture-facing periodic timer hook. It must be called every `USEC_PER_TICK`: [sched_processtimer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:162).

It performs all of the following:

- Advances wall/system time through `clock_update_wall_time()` and `clock_timer()`.
- Processes RR and sporadic scheduling for every configured CPU.
- Enters the SMP scheduler critical section because current TCBs across CPUs must remain stable.
- Expires watchdogs.
- Runs the optional board timer hook.

See [sched_processtimer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:179).

The ISR requirement is not incidental:

- Scheduler processing explicitly says it is executing in ISR context and uses `enter_critical_section()` for SMP stability: [sched_processtimer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:117).
- Watchdog callbacks are documented to run in the timer interrupt handler and are subject to ISR restrictions: [wd_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/wdog/wd_start.c:380).
- `wd_timer()` assumes interrupt-handler context with interrupts disabled: [wd_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/wdog/wd_start.c:400).

Authoritative examples call it directly:

- RP2040 SysTick ISR: [rp2040_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_timerisr.c:76).
- ESP32 timer ISR, including catch-up ticks: [esp32_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32/esp32_timerisr.c:68).
- Current BK7258 CPU0 SysTick ISR: [bk7258_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:39).

The only idle-loop call pattern found is for deliberately suppressed timer interrupts, where NuttX generates fake ticks: [arm_idle.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/common/arm_idle.c:47). It does not justify deferral in a normal SMP build.

Calling the full hook on both BK AP cores would also be unsafe: it would double global time, watchdog processing, and all-CPU scheduler accounting. CPU0-only ownership is correct.

**Atomic Contract**

`CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_HWSPINLOCK` means libc fallback atomics take a global `g_atomic_hwspinlock` with local IRQs disabled: [arch_atomic.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:324) and [hwspinlock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h:95).

Every fallback load, store, exchange, CAS, and fetch operation is serialized by that lock. The explicit memory-order argument is ignored because the lock provides stronger global serialization.

Reference implementations use actual hardware arbitration:

- RP2040 SIO spinlock: [rp2040_hwspinlock.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_hwspinlock.c:51).
- RP2040 global atomic lock instance: [rp2040_atomic.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_atomic.c:41).
- CXD56 SPH lock: [cxd56_hwspinlock.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/cxd56xx/cxd56_hwspinlock.c:51).

BK provides the required global instance at [bk7258_atomic.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_atomic.c:11), but its backend is a two-party Peterson gate rather than hardware arbitration: [bk7258_hwspinlock.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:25).

The linker/map evidence is internally consistent:

- Gate location is `0x28000000..0x28000014`.
- The section is dedicated `AP_SPINLOCK`.
- The MPU maps it inner-shareable and noncacheable: [bk7258_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:60).
- Linker assertions enforce placement: [ld.script](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/scripts/ld.script:141).
- The final map resolves `atomic_*_4`, `g_atomic_hwspinlock`, and the gate as intended: [nuttx.map](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map:6839).

Keeping that Peterson gate is a defensible short-term direction if the BK hardware truly lacks a usable AP hardware semaphore. It still needs two-core contention, recursion, interrupt-context, and prolonged SMP stress testing. Replacing it with `CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_IRQ` is unsafe because local IRQ masking does not serialize two CPUs. Switching to toolchain/exclusive-monitor atomics is also unsafe without hardware proof given the vendor warning about three active cores sharing only two exclusive monitors: [spinlock.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/spinlock/spinlock.c:136).

**Correct IPI Pattern**

The target interrupt handler must execute in IRQ context, drain SMP calls, and process delivered scheduler work. `nxsched_process_delivered()` explicitly asserts interrupt context: [sched_process_delivered.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_process_delivered.c:63).

Reference handlers consistently do both:

- RP2040: [rp2040_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_smpcall.c:91).
- ESP32 common handler: [xtensa_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/common/xtensa_smpcall.c:56).
- SAM4CM: [sam4cm_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/sam34/sam4cm_smpcall.c:69).

BK’s pending-bit multiplexing and handler order are compatible with that pattern: [bk7258_smpcall.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:169). The problem is transport progress, not the decision to distinguish CALL and SCHED bits.

Generic ARM-M `up_trigger_irq()` is not a remote IPI solution. It ignores `cpuset` and writes the local NVIC/STIR: [arm_trigger_irq.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_trigger_irq.c:50). BK must continue using a real cross-core mailbox/doorbell.

**History**

- `55e315e184143f1c7a77bb13c36c30973cb45abe`, dated 2026-08-04, added the mailbox console integration. Its timer remained the ARMv8-M generic SysTick lower-half and it did not contain the current SMP source files.
- `eaf469f1d36c739e9ff9de71350cace49909e791`, dated 2026-08-06, added Wi-Fi transport, enabled `CONFIG_SMP`, `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=2`, and `CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_HWSPINLOCK`, plus raw mailbox kick plumbing. It still retained the generic timer lower-half and referenced SMP files absent from the commit.
- The current direct CPU0 SysTick implementation, Peterson gate, CPU startup, and SMP-call implementation are post-`eaf469f` working-tree changes.
- The two NuttX snapshots have different repository heads, but the inspected RP2040, ESP32, and `arch_atomic.c` files are byte-identical. The contest NuttX tree alone has the local ticket-spinlock fix.

**Safe Minimal Directions**

- Keep one CPU0-owned SysTick and direct ISR invocation of `nxsched_process_timer()`.
- Keep CPU1’s private SysTick disabled.
- Ensure SysTick is enabled on CPU0 only, after CPU1 has reached scheduler-ready state and before any tick-based waits or periodic services are expected.
- Make cross-core IPI triggering non-droppable in both directions; persistent failure should be fatal, not silently converted into pending state.
- Once IPI triggering is reliable, remove timer-ISR responsibility for retrying SMP mailbox delivery.
- Preserve and commit the private-expected ticket-spinlock correction if `CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK` stays enabled.
- Commit the actual BK SMP/atomic source set so clean builds reproduce tested behavior.
- Retain the Peterson atomic gate until a documented BK hardware primitive is available, while adding contention and synchronous SMP-call stress validation.

**Unsafe Proposals**

- Moving `nxsched_process_timer()` or watchdog processing to a worker.
- Advancing clock time in ISR but deferring RR/sporadic scheduler processing without a NuttX scheduler redesign.
- Running the full timer hook on both AP CPUs.
- Using local IRQ masking as SMP atomicity.
- Switching back to `LDREX/STREX` or toolchain atomics solely because Cortex-M33 supports them.
- Treating a bounded mailbox retry failure as successful IPI delivery.
- Using generic local-NVIC `up_trigger_irq()` as a remote CPU interrupt.
- Starting SysTick via a synchronous SMP call during the secondary-core exception-return/startup window; the project’s own runtime notes record that approach as regressive: [README.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:694).

No files were changed. No runtime test was performed; the available `autoflash.log` records successful programming only and contains no sustained tick or SMP-call execution trace.
